c11_eng_s_cbse_01_004: Aram isn't blind to the code — his justifying proves he holds it. Check: why excuse what's not wrong?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_005: Mourad, Khosrove and Byro each carry a facet of the tribe — passion, trauma, reputation. Check: what does each represent?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_006: 'Stealing' is the plot — the theme is honesty tested and surviving. Check: act or insight?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_007: Poverty matters because honesty survives it — themes weave, they don't list. Check: how do they interact?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_008: 'The horse reared' is literal action — imagery must fire a sense. Check: felt or stated?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_009: 'I have a way with horses' is performance — Mourad plays the tribe's crazy heir. Check: boast or act?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_010: 'Capricious' links to 'vagrant' through 'and' — syntax pins the meaning, not the mood. Check: what's the local clue?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_011: 'Vazire, run' is intimacy in an imperative — grammar does narrative work. Check: what does the form achieve?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_012: 'He got scared' is a guess — his roar about the family name is the evidence. Check: which line supports it?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_013: 'I think he's crazy' is opinion — show how the text constructs the craziness. Check: reaction or mechanism?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_014: A diary isn't 'I rode, it was fun' — capture longing colliding with tribal pride. Check: where's the conflict?
c11_eng_s_cbse_01_015: 'Why did Aram fall off?' is recall — a discussion point must admit two readings. Check: is it arguable?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_001: Mrs Dorling isn't just greedy — she's 'Aryanisation' at kitchen-table scale. Check: individual or systemic?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_002: The flashbacks aren't filler — each lands to sharpen the contrast. Check: why placed there?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_003: The silver is the same — its tasteless new arrangement makes the air heavy. Check: what changed around it?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_004: Walking away isn't weakness — it's a chosen release from a dead past. Check: possession or freedom?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_005: No one here is pure — the mother's trust enabled the theft as much as Dorling's grip. Check: who made it possible?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_006: The war is backdrop — the theme is discovering objects can't carry memory. Check: external event or inner turn?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_007: 'The silver' is a subject — 'objects severed from people lose meaning' is a theme. Check: noun or claim?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_008: The cardigan looks right but feels wrong — that gap enacts her dissociation. Check: seen or felt?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_009: The cold refusal isn't irony — her changed bond with the objects is. Check: what reversed?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_010: 'Crick' is the mother's homely word — vocabulary carries class and voice. Check: whose word is it?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_011: Don't just label the past perfect — it holds the pre-war world at a distance. Check: what does it keep separate?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_012: 'She liked it' is a guess — the burn mark and pattern tell why she rubbed it. Check: which details?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_013: The story never says 'Holocaust' — it's about objects failing across rupture. Check: history lesson or memory study?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_014: 'Today I went to Marconi Street' is narration — make a claim and prove it. Check: event or argument?
c11_eng_s_cbse_02_015: Plot points aren't discussion — ask why the two visits are built differently. Check: what or why?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_001: Context isn't just dates — it's the one-act form, 1950s suburbia, Priestley's socialism. Check: which lens?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_002: The magic doesn't fix anything — it lets you watch the decision work. Check: solution or enactment?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_003: The armchair holds two different mothers — behaviour, not décor, shifts the air. Check: what changed in the room?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_004: The swap doesn't give her a spine — it shows the spine she already had. Check: whose choice at the end?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_005: In a five-person play, nobody is minor — Doris, Cyril, George each embody a pressure. Check: what does each stand for?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_006: It isn't a friendship lesson — the family responds rationally to absent boundaries. Check: who's the real agent?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_007: 'Smoking' is a prop — 'bodily autonomy as resistance' is the theme. Check: what's it saying about it?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_008: Devices fuse here — 'flurried tone' is sound that encodes her weightlessness. Check: fused or separate?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_009: The swap isn't fantasy — it makes her servitude strange and visible. Check: who knows what the family doesn't?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_010: 'Silly' from the swapped mother is a threat, not a tease — speaker changes meaning. Check: who says it, to whom?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_011: Imperatives aren't just grammar — they're who's allowed to command. Check: what power does the form carry?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_012: 'I think she's brave' needs a line — cite the moment that proves it. Check: which stage direction?
c11_eng_s_cbse_03_013: 'Body-swaps aren't real' isn't criticism — the device argues how deep the scripts run. Check: objection or analysis?
